body:
Did a quick test, some feedback:

- The size of the preview sphere should be configurable in project settings to make it usable in projects that don't use human scale
- When the node is selected it would be cleaner to disable the 2D icon because most of the time it will be partially or fully behind the preview sphere
- It would be nice to show more than one preview at a time for multiple selected nodes because it's possible to modify properties of multiple reflection probes at once in inspector

> The size of the preview sphere should be configurable in project settings to make it usable in projects that don't use human scale

I'm wondering if it would make sense to have the sphere's size be determined by a screen-space size, like gizmo icons. Even within single projects reflection probe sizes can vary greatly. If a user has probe covering a large area they are much more likely to be further away from the probes center/capture point compared to if they're tweaking a probe in a small room.

> I'm wondering if it would make sense to have the sphere's size be determined by a screen-space size, like gizmo icons.

I tried it when I made the addon and didn't like it. Preview spheres rendered like regular objects in world scale means you can put your face close to them to better examine the cubemap. It feels natural to be able to do that.

> Even within single projects reflection probe sizes can vary greatly. If a user has probe covering a large area they are much more likely to be further away from the probes center/capture point compared to if they're tweaking a probe in a small room.

This seems unrelated to your previous comment about the fixed screen size. If we make preview spheres depend on the probe size they still don't need to be of fixed screen size. I'm not sure if we should do that though, it's hard to tell without testing that.

> This seems unrelated to your previous comment about the fixed screen size.

I meant to illustrate that chances are higher that your view is further away from the preview sphere if you have a large probe. If that preview sphere has a fixed world size it might become quite small on screen, and I suspect you wouldn't be able to get a great feel for the reflection result at a glance. With a screen-space size this wouldn't be a concern.


> I tried it when I made the addon and didn't like it. Preview spheres rendered like regular objects in world scale means you can put your face close to them to better examine the cubemap. It feels natural to be able to do that.

This makes sense. Could a combination of the two make sense? A world-space size with a minimum screen-space size, allowing you to still get up close?

I do feel like something that adjusts to the view distance would make sense since we cannot reasonably predict or make assumptions about the scales used in projects. I'm a little wary of setting a gizmo size default on the assumption of first/third person game scale, because while projects rarely go smaller in unit size, they do often go larger.

That said, I don't feel _super_ strongly about this, I'm happy to concede my position on this. We can stay with world-space size, validate how that experience is, and adjust if needed.

> I do feel like something that adjusts to the view distance would make sense since we cannot reasonably predict or make assumptions about the scales used in projects.

I personally [agree with WickedInsignia](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/10018#issuecomment-2620203083) that we can make an assumption that most genres revolve around human scale and it makes sense to design editor UX with that default in mind, and for reflection probes I feel like it's an even safer assumption because for very large worlds you are less likely to rely on probes in the first place because you would need too many of them in the scene. You'd probably need a more scalable solution that doesn't rely on baking cubemaps in those projects.

> Could a combination of the two make sense? A world-space size with a minimum screen-space size, allowing you to still get up close

Maybe, my biggest concern though is how intuitive that would be. The linked proposal above discusses doing the opposite for gizmos - rendering with fixed size when close and world size when far away. If gizmos and previews behave in opposite ways wouldn't it feel weird? It's hard to say without testing
